candidates.statement: EMA/169546/2012 Page 3/11 X.A. Introduction 38 Pharmacovigilance is a vital public health function with the aim of rapidly detecting and responding to 39 potential safety hazards associated with the use of medicinal products. 40 A medicinal product is authorised on the basis that in the specified indication(s), at the time of 41 authorisation, the risk-benefit balance is judged to be positive for the target population. However, not 42 all risks can be identified at the time when an initial authorisation is sought and many of the risks 43 associated with the use of a medicinal product can only be discovered or fully characterised post- 44 authorisation. To strengthen the safety monitoring of medicinal products, the 2010 EU 45 Pharmacovigilance legislation has introduced a framework for enhanced risk proportionate post- 46 authorisation data collection for medicinal products, one element of which is the concept of additional 47 monitoring for certain medicinal products. 48 As defined in Article 23 of Regulation (EC) No 726/2004, the Agency shall, in collaboration with the 49 Member States, set up, maintain and make public a list of medicinal products that are subject to 50 additional monitoring (hereafter referred to as “the list”). These medicinal products will be readily 51 identifiable by the introduction of the statement “This medicinal product is subject to additional 52 monitoring” preceded by a standard black symbol and followed by an appropriate standardised 53 explanatory statement in their summary of product characteristics (SmPC) and package leaflets (PL). 54 This explanatory statement should encourage healthcare professionals and patients to report all 55

suspected adverse reactions. 56 Post-authorisation spontaneous adverse reaction reports remain a cornerstone of pharmacovigilance. 57 Data from spontaneous suspected adverse drug reactions (ADR) is a key source of information for 58 signal detection activities (see Module IX). Increasing the awareness of healthcare professionals and 59 patients of the need to report suspected adverse reactions and encouraging their reporting is therefore 60 a potentially important means of monitoring the safe use of a medicinal product. 61 The concept of additional monitoring originates primarily from the need to increase the proportionality 62 between ADR reporting and the level of knowledge about the safety of a product and to allow a 63 differentiated view of specific medicines. The main goals are to collect additional information as early 64 as possible to further elucidate the risk profile of products when used in clinical practice and to 65 increase awareness about the safe and effective use of certain medicinal products. It is important to 66 emphasize, however, that this concept does not lead to earlier granting of a marketing authorisation. 67 This Module is divided in two sections: 68 • section X.B. provides general principles for assigning additional monitoring status to medicinal 69 products and on the communication and transparency aspects. 70 • section X.C. describes the operation of the EU network regarding the supervision of additional 71 monitoring status, the communication strategy and the impact on pharmacovigilance activities. 72 X.B. Structures and processes 73 X.B.1. General principles for assigning additional monitoring status to a 74 medicinal product 75

Communication and transparency 98 The additional monitoring status needs to be communicated to healthcare professionals and patients in 99 such a way that it increases reporting of suspected adverse reactions but without creating undue 100 alarm. A publicly available list of medicinal products with additional monitoring status should be kept 101 up to date by the competent authorities. In addition, healthcare professionals and patients should be 102 enabled to easily identify those products through their product labelling. The publication of the list 103 together with appropriate communication should encourage healthcare professionals and patients to 104 report all suspected adverse reactions while supervising or receiving treatment with a medicinal 105 product subject to additional monitoring. 106 X.B.3. Quality systems and record management 107 An essential feature of the process for the creation and maintenance of the list and for the 108 communication of the status of additional monitoring is that it is clearly documented to ensure that the 109 system functions properly and effectively, that the roles, responsibilities and required tasks are 110 conducted in a timely manner and are clear to all parties involved. Therefore, a system of quality 111 assurance and quality control consistent with the quality system standards should be in place and 112 applied to processes (see Module I). 113 Detailed procedures for this quality system should be devised, documented and implemented. The 114

Therefore, after a medicine is placed on the market, its use in the 82 wider population requires continuous monitoring. As for all medicinal products, marketing 83 authorisation holders and competent authorities continuously monitor any information that becomes 84 available and assess the impact on the risk-benefit profile of the medicinal product. However, for 85 certain medicinal products enhanced post-authorisation data collection is needed to ensure that any 86 new safety hazards are identified as promptly as possible and that appropriate action can be initiated 87 immediately. candidates.statement: 21 July 2012 [DIR Art 104a]. 154 The scope of Article 23(2) of Regulation (EC) No 726/2004 does not only include medicinal products 155 which are authorised or for which conditions are established after entry into force of the new 156 pharmacovigilance legislation but also medicinal products which were authorised or made subject to 157 conditions before such date, provided they fall within one or more of the above described situations. 158 Pharmacovigilance rules in general and additional monitoring specifically take into account that the full 159 safety profile of medicinal products can only be confirmed after products have been placed on the 160 market. Due consideration should, therefore, be given to the merit of inclusion of a medicinal product 161 in the list in terms of increasing awareness about the safe and effective use of a medicinal product 162 and/or providing any additional information for the evaluation of the product. In this regard, the 163 decision to include a medicinal product subject to conditions in the list should take account of the 164 nature and scope of the conditions or obligations placed on the marketing authorisation including their 165 potential public health impact. The decision should also consider the usefulness of the additional 166 monitoring status in relation to other additional pharmacovigilance activities proposed in the risk 167 management plan, for example in relation to the objectives of post-authorisation safety studies 168 (PASS). 169 If a reference medicinal product that is subject to conditions is included in the list, due consideration 170

Mandatory scope 191 In the case where a medicinal product is automatically included in the list at the time of granting of the 192 marketing authorisation, consideration of removal from the list at the five year time point will normally 193 be linked with the renewal procedure. In cases where the removal of a medicinal product from the list 194 cannot be linked with the renewal procedure (e.g. informed consent or duplicate applications), the 195 product will be removed from the list by default 5 years after the URD, unless a different decision has 196 been taken during the renewal of the first medicinal product authorised in EU containing the same 197 active substance. During the renewal, the European Commission or the national competent authority, 198 as appropriate, should indicate if the medicinal product should be maintained in the list if justified in 199 terms of increasing awareness about the safe and effective use of a medicinal product and/or providing 200 any additional information for the evaluation of the product. The criteria for extending the period of 201 inclusion should take into account the frequency of submission of PSURs and the need for an additional 202 renewal. Black symbol and explanatory statements 350 For medicinal products included in the list, the SmPC and the package leaflet shall include the 351 statement “This medicinal product is subject to additional monitoring”. This statement shall be 352 preceded by a black symbol, which is selected by the European Commission on the basis of a 353 recommendation by the PRAC and followed by an explanatory sentence explaining the concept of 354 additional monitoring. 355 Once the medicinal product is included or removed from the list, the marketing authorisation holder 356 shall update the SmPC and the package leaflet to include or remove, as appropriate, the black symbol, 357 the statement, and the standardised explanatory statement. 358 If the decision to include or remove a medicinal product from the list is done during the assessment of 359 a regulatory procedure (e.g. marketing authorisation application, extension of indication, renewal) the 360 SmPC and the package leaflet should be updated before finalisation of the procedure in order to 361 include or remove, as appropriate, the statement, the black symbol and explanatory statement from 362 the product information. If the decision to include or remove a medicinal product from the list is done 363 outside a regulatory procedure, then the marketing authorisation holder is requested to subsequently 364 submit the relevant variation to include or remove, as appropriate, the black symbol, the statement, 365 and the standardised explanatory statement. 366 X.C.7.
